summary:
ROOT CAUSE (reproduced and confirmed): NaN pixels from zero-area triangles that carry zero-length vertex normals, mostly on the Porsche GT3 RS exhibit (worst is the front splitter) and the circuit kerbs next to it. The bloom pass then spreads each NaN pixel into a huge black rectangle. The firefly-clamp ShaderPass in src/main.js:330-340 is meant to protect the bloom but lets NaN through.

The chain:
(1) src/vehicles/gt3rs.js:1655-1665 buildSplitter builds its outline from side points clamped with Math.min(halfW(x)*0.97, W). That gives a run of collinear points along z=±W (±0.825 m). ExtrudeGeometry/earcut turns them into 20 triangles of exactly zero area, up to 0.19 m long, whose computeVertexNormals normals are (0,0,0).
(2) Once transformed in float32 on the GPU, these slivers occasionally rasterise a single pixel. In the lit shader, normalize(vec3(0)) gives NaN, so that pixel's HDR colour is NaN.
(3) The firefly clamp lets NaN straight through: `m > uPeak` is false for NaN. It also turns any Inf (half-float overflow) into NaN, because c.rgb*(uPeak/Inf) = Inf*0.
(4) UnrealBloomPass's separable blur over 5 mips (kernel up to 11 taps at 1/32 resolution) spreads that one NaN into a rectangle hundreds of pixels wide. OutputPass writes NaN as black.
(5) The sliver pixel appears in some frames and not others as the camera or car moves, so the black block flickers very fast.

EVIDENCE:
- Float32 renders of orbit views around the H2R (centre -580.5, 0.1, -236.0) had 1-2 NaN pixels in 13 of the views logged (≈85 views rendered before I stopped the sweep).
- Ray-pick plus hide-one-mesh elimination at 4 of those views. In 3 of them the only culprit was 'gt3-splitter<gt3-sprung<gt3rs' (material gt3-black-plastic, face 127); hiding it brings the NaN count to 0. The 4th view hit Starship's 'tanks' far in the background, a separate NaN source that the shader fix also covers.
- Full-pipeline test with composer MSAA off, at the 3 splitter views: 281,700 / 296,100 / 295,650 of 360,000 pixels exactly black. The black regions are solid rectangles reaching the frame edges, e.g. box [0,0,625,449] on an 800x450 frame.
- Attribution:
  - bloom disabled: 76/52/41 black pixels (normal);
  - AO disabled: unchanged (AO is not involved);
  - a forced single NaN quad: 360,000/360,000 black with bloom, 18 without.
- Flicker: 40 consecutive frames orbiting 0.5° per frame gave `.X...XXX..X.XXX.X.XXX.XXX..X.X..XX......` (X = black block).
- Both fixes tested in the page: the NaN-safe clamp, and the splitter's 20 zero-normal triangles removed (228 of 248 left). Each brings all 3 views to 0 black pixels.
- Scene-wide scan after boot: 41 lit meshes contain triangles with zero-length vertex normals, 495 triangles in all. Almost all are in the Porsche area:
  - gt3-cabin-gloss-x 80, carbon-x 50, carpet-x 38, black-x 36, alu-x 10, leather-x 4;
  - gt3-openings 36, gt3-wheel-black 20, gt3-splitter 20;
  - circuit-kerb-0..25 with 6 each;
  - lamp bowls/lenses, black-trim and seat buckles 2 each;
  - plus the Roadster's body-paint 35.
  The H2R itself has none.
- Caveat: SwiftShader's MSAA resolve drops NaN. With the shipped msaa:4 my headless frames showed no black block, even with a forced NaN quad. I had to set composer.renderTarget1/2.samples=0 to reproduce. On real GPUs a multisample resolve generally averages arithmetically and keeps NaN, which matches the user's report on the high/medium tiers. The low tier has no bloom, so there it would only be a single black pixel.

HYPOTHESES TESTED AND RULED OUT as the cause:
- Tyre smoke and spray: the black block appears in static exhibit views with no drive running. Their gl_PointSize is unclamped (src/sim/gt3Drive.js:95 and :146, size*600/max(0.5,-mv.z), up to ≈4,400 px within 0.5 m), but they draw light-grey translucent discs, not black squares. Worth clamping like src/core/effects.js:36 as hygiene.
- core/effects.js: already clamped to 1..512.
- Skid-mark ring buffer: no NaN path; positions come only from contact points.
- HUD canvases (src/ui/gt3Hud.js:147, h2rHud.js:152): the telemetry box is a steady rgba(10,12,14,0.5) panel, not a flicker.
- GTAO: disabling it changed nothing.
- HDR overflow: the maximum scene radiance seen was 3,819, below half-float's 65,504, so no Inf in these views. The clamp's Inf→NaN is still a latent bug and the fix covers it.
- The H2R screen material (h2rBody.js:180-181): not hit in any NaN pick.
- LOD, shadows, z-fighting: they cannot produce NaN, and the elimination test isolated a single mesh.

Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-spacex/49448258-b837-551e-9b35-7fac201f56d4/scratchpad/diag/blk/: sweep2.mjs (orbit sweep with per-pass half-float NaN readback), probe.mjs (NaN pixel → mesh), prop2.mjs (attribution and both fixes), flicker.mjs (consecutive frames), scan_scene.mjs (scene-wide zero-normal scan), tri.mjs (degenerate triangles per mesh, Node). Logs: sw2.log.

findings.title: Firefly clamp before bloom passes NaN and turns Inf into NaN; bloom spreads one NaN pixel into a flickering black rectangle
findings.evidence: src/main.js:330-340: `float m = max(max(c.r,c.g),c.b); gl_FragColor = vec4(m > uPeak ? c.rgb * (uPeak / m) : c.rgb, c.a);`. For NaN, `m > uPeak` is false, so NaN goes through. For Inf, c*(12/Inf) = Inf*0 = NaN. UnrealBloomPass (main.js:322, :342) blurs it over 5 mips. Composer MSAA off at splitter views: 281,700-296,100 of 360,000 px black in solid rectangles. A forced NaN quad blacks out 100% of the frame with bloom and 18 px without. Replacing the clamp shader with a NaN/Inf-safe version gave 0 black px at all 3 views (in-page test, prop2.mjs).
findings.fix: Replace the fragmentShader at main.js:334-339 with: `uniform sampler2D tDiffuse; uniform float uPeak; varying vec2 vUv; void main() { vec4 c = texture2D(tDiffuse, vUv); if (any(isnan(c.rgb)) || any(isinf(c.rgb))) c.rgb = vec3(0.0); if (isnan(c.a)) c.a = 1.0; float m = max(max(c.r, c.g), c.b); gl_FragColor = vec4(m > uPeak ? c.rgb * (uPeak / m) : c.rgb, c.a); }`. This is WebGL2 GLSL ES 3.00, where isnan/isinf exist; it compiled and worked in the test. Update the comment above (main.js:323-329) to say the pass also drops non-finite pixels: a zero-length normal or a half-float overflow, which the bloom would otherwise print as a black block. Optional: add the same pass when bloom is off, so a NaN never reaches OutputPass as a stray pixel.

findings.title: Zero-area triangles with zero-length normals in the GT3 RS front splitter (collinear outline points) rasterise NaN pixels
findings.evidence: gt3rs.js:1655-1665 buildSplitter: `side = range(1.85, X_NOSE, 10).map(x => [x, Math.min(halfW(x)*0.97, W)])` clamps several consecutive points to z=W, so they are collinear. ExtrudeGeometry then yields 20 of 248 triangles with area exactly 0, edges up to 0.1865 m, at z=-0.825 / y 0.122-0.14, all three vertex normals (0,0,0) (tri.mjs). Ray-pick plus hide-one elimination at 3 NaN views: only 'gt3-splitter' (gt3-black-plastic, face 127); hiding it drops the NaN count to 0. Removing those 20 triangles cleared the black blocks at all 3 views.
findings.fix: Before `new THREE.Shape(...)` in buildSplitter, drop duplicate and collinear outline points: `const clean = outline.filter((p, i, a) => { const q = a[(i + a.length - 1) % a.length], r = a[(i + 1) % a.length]; const cr = (p[0]-q[0])*(r[1]-p[1]) - (p[1]-q[1])*(r[0]-p[0]); return Math.hypot(p[0]-q[0], p[1]-q[1]) > 1e-6 && Math.abs(cr) > 1e-9; });` and build the shape from `clean`. The splitter's shape does not change: only redundant vertices go.

findings.title: Many other meshes in the Porsche area (cabin, openings, steering wheel, kerbs) and the Roadster also have zero-normal sliver triangles
findings.fix:
Add a build-time sanitizer to src/geometry/utils.js and call it once in main.js just before `hud.setProgress('Compiling shaders…', 0.95)` (main.js:851): `sanitizeNormals(scene)`. Implementation:
- Traverse the meshes and keep a Set of geometries already done.
- For each triangle (index or 3t..3t+2), flag it when any vertex normal has squared length <= 1e-12 or is non-finite.
- Compute the face normal from the float32 positions.
- If its length is > 1e-12 (a real triangle whose vertex normal cancelled out), write the face normal into the bad vertices.
- Otherwise collapse the triangle exactly: indexed geometry → setX on the index so all three corners equal i0; non-indexed → copy the position of i0 into i1 and i2, and set the three normals to (0,1,0). Identical vertices can never rasterise.
- Mark position, normal and index needsUpdate.
This keeps vertex and triangle counts, groups and draw ranges unchanged, so the check.mjs triangle budget is unaffected. Return the count, and log it in dev only.

findings.title: Tyre smoke / spray point size unclamped
findings.evidence: gt3Drive.js:95 and :146 use `gl_PointSize = size * scale / max(0.5, -mv.z)` with no clamp. Smoke size reaches 3.7, so ≈4,400 px when a puff is within 0.5 m of the camera, which is above most GPUs' point-size limit. This is not the black square (the sprites are light grey and translucent), but it is inconsistent with core/effects.js:36.
findings.fix: Wrap both in `clamp(..., 1.0, 512.0)`, as effects.js:36 does.

plan:
FIX (one commit; run `npm run check:static` first, then the full check per CLAUDE.md):
1. src/main.js:334-339: make the firefly clamp NaN/Inf-safe. Shader text is in finding 1: `if (any(isnan(c.rgb)) || any(isinf(c.rgb))) c.rgb = vec3(0.0); if (isnan(c.a)) c.a = 1.0;` before computing m. Extend the comment at :323-329 to say why. This is the hot fix: it stops every NaN source (geometry, the Starship tanks NaN, half-float overflow) from turning into a block.
2. src/vehicles/gt3rs.js:1655-1665 buildSplitter: filter duplicate and collinear outline points before building the Shape (code in finding 2).
3. src/geometry/utils.js: add `export function sanitizeNormals(root)`. It fixes zero normals on real triangles with the face normal and collapses true zero-area triangles to a single vertex, keeping counts. Call it in src/main.js right before `hud.setProgress('Compiling shaders…', 0.95)` (line 851). Algorithm in finding 3.
4. Optional hygiene: clamp gl_PointSize in src/sim/gt3Drive.js:95 and :146 to [1, 512].
5. README (Spanish): short section describing the bug (black block flickering near the Porsche and H2R), the cause (NaN from a zero normal, spread by the bloom) and the fix. Add a TRASPASO lesson: never let a pass before the bloom pass NaN through; avoid collinear points in ExtrudeGeometry outlines.

REGRESSION CHECKS (add to tools/check.mjs next to the "No stencil on the multisampled composer targets" block, check.mjs ≈ line 905-918; messages in Spanish like the others):
A) "ningún triángulo iluminado con normal nula". In page.evaluate:
   - traverse window.__vc.scene;
   - for meshes with a normal attribute and a non-Basic, non-Shader material, count triangles where any vertex normal has squared length <= 1e-12 or is non-finite, unless the triangle is collapsed (all three positions identical);
   - report(count === 0), listing the first 5 mesh names.
   Today this gives 495 triangles in 41 meshes; after step 3 it must give 0.
B) "un píxel NaN no se convierte en un bloque negro":
   - const c = v.composer, s0 = c.renderTarget1.samples;
   - set c.renderTarget1.samples = c.renderTarget2.samples = 0 and dispose() both. This is needed because SwiftShader's MSAA resolve swallows NaN, so with MSAA the test would pass even when broken.
   - jump('h2r','overview'); add a 4 mm PlaneGeometry 2 m in front of the camera with a ShaderMaterial whose fragment shader is `uniform float z; void main(){ float n = z / z; gl_FragColor = vec4(n, n, n, 1.0); }` (uniform z = 0, so it cannot be constant-folded);
   - camera.updateMatrixWorld(); c.render(); gl.readPixels the whole drawing buffer in the same task;
   - count pixels with r, g, b <= 1;
   - remove the quad, restore the samples to s0 and dispose both targets again so they are rebuilt with MSAA.
   - Assert black pixels < 1% of the frame: today 100% (360,000/360,000 at 800x450); after the fix about 0.
   - Skip when quality.bloom is false.
C) Optional static check (Node, part of check:static via tools/gt3rs-check.mjs): build buildGt3rs with a Proxy materials object, as in scratch tri.mjs, run sanitizeNormals on the result, then assert no zero-normal triangles. 'gt3-splitter' must have 0 even before the sanitizer, which proves the source fix.

MANUAL VERIFICATION (headless): with the scratch script diag/blk/flicker.mjs (40 frames orbiting the H2R at 5 m, composer MSAA off), today's pattern is `.X...XXX..X.XXX.X.XXX.XXX..X.X..XX......`; after the fix it must be all dots. diag/blk/prop2.mjs shows the before/after numbers per view.
